evals.prompt: Use Three.js to make a responsive single-file HTML landing page with an animated 3D product hero, headline, call-to-action, keyboard-accessible controls, and a mobile fallback. Use CSS and vanilla JavaScript and verify it in a browser.
evals.expected_output: A coordinated implementation that loads threejs-development as the scene owner while frontend-design owns the semantic page shell, responsive DOM composition, controls, content hierarchy, and accessible fallback; CSS and JavaScript remain supporting boundaries.
assertions: The response does not treat the request as an ordinary frontend-only page after Three.js is explicitly named.
It loads or routes through threejs-development before defining renderer, scene, camera, animation, resources, or 3D verification.
Frontend ownership remains limited to semantic HTML, content hierarchy, responsive DOM, controls, state presentation, and accessible fallback.
The implementation preserves the requested single-file delivery unless a different setup is explicitly justified.
Browser verification covers the rendered scene, resize, narrow viewport, keyboard path, reduced motion, console errors, and fallback behavior.

evals.prompt: This website looks generic. Modify the existing frontend so it feels polished and professional without changing product behavior.
evals.expected_output: A frontend-design-led implementation that inspects the existing surface, preserves behavior, makes bounded visual decisions, changes the visible UI, and verifies representative states and viewports without requiring a separate design-direction phase.
assertions: The response treats frontend-design as the baseline even though the request uses vague language such as polished and professional.
It does not block implementation merely because a separate visual direction was not supplied.
It preserves existing behavior and design-system evidence before making bounded visual changes.
It verifies the rendered interface rather than relying only on compilation.

evals.prompt: Fix the CSS spacing, typography, card alignment, and mobile overflow on this page while preserving its HTML and behavior.
evals.expected_output: A coordinated visible-UI fix in which frontend-design owns the complete page contract and css-development owns CSS mechanics, with responsive and rendered-state verification.
assertions: The response loads frontend-design as the visible UI baseline.
It uses css-development as an additive specialist rather than a replacement.
It preserves HTML and product behavior.
It verifies layout at narrow and desktop viewports.

evals.prompt: Restyle this React settings page and improve its forms, buttons, spacing, loading, error, disabled, and focus states.
evals.expected_output: A frontend-design-led React UI implementation that adds only the required React state, styling, and accessibility specialists while preserving component and data behavior.
assertions: The response loads frontend-design as the baseline for the visible React UI change.
React or styling specialists supplement rather than replace frontend-design.
Loading, error, disabled, and focus states are implemented and verified.
The response preserves existing data and event contracts.

evals.prompt: Fix this frontend table so it no longer overflows on mobile, its filters reflow cleanly, and controls remain usable without reducing desktop information density.
evals.expected_output: A frontend-design-led responsive implementation that uses responsive-design and CSS support for intentional reflow, touch targets, overflow, and representative viewport verification.
assertions: The response loads frontend-design as the visible UI baseline.
Responsive specialists remain additive.
The solution reflows content instead of merely shrinking the desktop UI.
Verification covers narrow, intermediate, and desktop widths.

evals.prompt: Implement a FastAPI endpoint that validates a request, writes one database record transactionally, and returns a typed response. No frontend is involved.
evals.expected_output: A backend-only implementation route that does not load or claim frontend-design ownership.
assertions: The response does not load frontend-design.
It keeps ownership within Python backend, validation, persistence, and testing boundaries.
It does not invent a web interface.

evals.prompt: The repository has a three dependency used by another route. Fix the ordinary login form typography and focus styling; no canvas or scene contract is affected.
evals.expected_output: A frontend and CSS task without an unrelated 3D owner.
assertions: It retains frontend-design for visible UI behavior and verification.
It does not load Three.js Skills based only on dependency presence.
It preserves the form's behavior and accessibility.

evals.prompt: Build a plain Canvas 2D bar chart with accessible DOM labels. Do not use WebGL or Three.js.
evals.expected_output: A semantic frontend implementation with 2D canvas ownership.
assertions: It respects the explicit Canvas 2D requirement.
It does not route generic canvas wording to Three.js.
It verifies labels, rendering, and relevant responsive behavior.
